response: {"headline": "SOLID-TIMI 52 failed to show darapladib reduces major coronary events after acute coronary syndrome, consistent with a non-causal Lp-PLA2 target.", "summary": "The SOLID-TIMI 52 trial randomized 13,026 patients after acute coronary syndrome to darapladib 160 mg or placebo, targeting a 15.5% relative risk reduction with 90% power and 1,500 planned primary endpoint events over a median 3-year follow-up. The trial did not meet its primary endpoint of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (GSK announcement, 13 May 2014). Genetic evidence shows no causal link between PLA2G7 and coronary heart disease (Open Targets score 0.0), and the calculator predicts no benefit (expected HR 1.0, causal RRR 0%, probability of success 2.5%). Despite robust Lp-PLA2 inhibition of 59–81% in phase 2 studies, the biomarker reduction did not translate to clinical benefit. Safety was acceptable with no major concerns. Confidence in the failure assessment is medium.", "key_evidence": ["13,026 participants randomized (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01000727 SOLID-TIMI 52)", "Primary endpoint: composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome)", "1,500 planned primary endpoint events (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome)", "90% power (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome)", "Assumed 15.5% relative risk reduction (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome)", "Planned median follow-up: 3 years (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome)", "Readout: darapladib did not achieve the primary endpoint of a reduction of major coronary events versus placebo (GSK announces phase III study with darapladib did not meet primary endpoint in patients following an acute coronary syndrome (13 May 2014))", "Lp-PLA2 inhibition 59–81% in phase 2 studies (multiple sources including Effect of darapladib treatment on endarterectomy carotid plaque lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 activity: a randomized, controlled trial; Peripheral artery disease, biomarkers, and darapladib)", "PLA2G7 genetic association score 0.0 (opentargets:PLA2G7)", "Calculator: expected HR 1.0, causal RRR 0.0%, probability of success 2.5% (calculator)"], "what_would_change_this": "A positive result would require human genetic evidence supporting PLA2G7 as a causal target for coronary events, or a different patient population or endpoint where Lp-PLA2 inhibition shows a clear mechanistic link to outcomes.", "readthrough_note": "The companion STABILITY trial in stable coronary heart disease (NCT00799903) also failed (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.85–1.03), reinforcing that Lp-PLA2 inhibition with darapladib does not reduce cardiovascular events across ACS and stable CHD populations."}
